articleTitle: A Fast Graph Minor Embedding Heuristic for Oscillator Based Ising Machines
abstract: The demand for high-efficient computing power is constantly increasing. While digital CMOS designs are dom-inating, more research is focusing on novel computing ar-chitectures. Recently, so-called Oscillator-based Ising Machines (OIMs) have become a promising computing approach, which can solve optimization problems using configurable coupling between oscillators. OIMs are based on well-established CMOS silicon technologies and can even be integrated with a processor as hard-ware accelerators. Similarly to quantum computing, OIMs solve graph problems by directly representing them in their hardware. Consequently, the nodes and edges of a problem graph must be mapped to the available hardware-specific network. Since such graph embedding is required before every computation, it has a crucial impact on performance. We propose a heuristic embedding algorithm to transform quickly and efficiently an input problem onto a target hardware. The heuristic is optimized for OIM systems and supports various hardware topologies including routing channels. Using the heuristic algorithm, we analyze different hardware topologies to further improve OIM designs.

articleTitle: A Low-Noise Transconductance Amplifier (LNTA) for Cryogenic Applications using CMOS Technology
abstract: Quantum computing is the most prominent field in cryogenic applications. And they use room temperature classical electronic controllers for qubit read-out and control, which are bulky and complex, and limit the number of effective qubits to operate. There is a need for a higher level of integration and a large number of qubit operations, so the validation of CMOS technology at cryogenic temperature is required. This paper presents the study of device characteristics and design parameter variation of 180nm NMOS device. Also, the low noise transconductance amplifier is designed and simulated for noise performance at room temperature 300K and at cryogenic temperature 4K. The proposed design shows the noise figure of 5.3 dB and 0.272 dB at 300K and 4K, respectively. Also, it achieves the S21 of 14.4 dB and 17.4 dB at 300K and 4K, respectively with IIP3 of 19.64 dBm at 4K. This opens the scope for designing a CMOS qubit controller at cryogenic temperature in addition to the high level of integration.

articleTitle: Reduction of the Critical Path of IIR Filters using Continued Fractions
abstract: Implementing infinite impulse response (IIR) filters as synchronous sequential circuits is common practice in dig-ital signal processing. In this paper, a decomposition of IIR filter transfer functions in order to reduce the critical path in comparison to the canonical form (transposed direct form II) implementation based on continued fractions is discussed. Moreover, the filtered quantization noise of the resulting con-tinued fraction structure is analyzed. The coefficients of the IIR filters are quantized with the canonical signed digit (CSD) representation. An adder tree structure has been used for the implementation of the multiplications. The continued fraction structure and the canonical form have been implemented in VHDL and synthesized for the Intel Cyclone V FPGA. The synthesis results of the continued fraction structure feature an increased maximum clock frequency in comparison with the canonical form implementation. However, the resource utilization of the continued fraction structure is significantly increased compared to the canonical form implementation. The filtered quantization noise of the continued fraction structure is decreased in comparison to the canonical form implementation.

articleTitle: Digital Pre-Distortion for CS- DACs based on Inverse Modelling of Volterra Series Expansion
abstract: This paper presents a dynamic digital pre-distortion (DPD) method for a current-steering digital-to-analog converter (CS-DAC). The novel proposed method is based on the inverse modelling of a Volterra series expansion of the system. It uses a memory structure often only used for DPD in power amplifiers (PA). The goal is to find a model with minimal parameter count to counteract the signal dependent non-linearites of charge injection from the switching activity of the converter. A priori knowledge of the non-linear behavior and architecture of the DAC is exploited. The DPD uses an indirect learning architecture to generate the inverse system. The proposed Volterra system consists of a first and third order kernel with a respective memory depth of one. This results in a total number of 6 parameters that need to be estimated. This is sufficient to significantly attenuate the non-linear distortions. The evaluation of the proposed DPD is done via Spice simulations of a 14-bit lumped model of the CS-DAC. Small and wideband discrete multi-tone (DMT) signals with a frequency of up to 684 MHz are simulated. The results show a performance gain of the missing-tone-power-ratio MTPR of up 8.4dB.

articleTitle: An Unbiased MEMS Capacitance-Controlled Oscillator as a Microphone for HMI Applications
abstract: MEMS microphones are usually DC biased with a voltage exceeding 10V and a large resistance, requiring a charge pump and a high-ohmic link between the ASIC and the MEMS. This DC biasing is needed to obtain enough sensitivity for medium to high quality microphones. This manuscript inves-tigates capacitance-controlled oscillators which allow to directly connect the MEMS sensor to the oscillator; this solution is prone to scaling. A new type of configuration (referred to as Cross-Connected Sensor) is presented and discussed. Its main advantage is the increase in the sensitivity and, when integrated in an ADC architecture, in the achievable SNR. The proposed solution is intended for Human-Machine Interface applications given their moderate SNR requirements.

articleTitle: Comparison of Simulation and Measurement of EMI-Induced Offset Voltages Occuring at Folded Cascode Operational Amplifiers
abstract: In this paper we address the simulated and mea-sured electromagnetic interference (EMI) behaviour of integrated folded cascode amplifiers. We compare the EMI-induced offset voltages at different frequencies. Therefore, we determine these EMI-induced offset voltages on the one hand by measurements and on the other hand by various simulation methods. We take different simulation variants into account, for example considering layout parasitics, package parasitics, process corners, as well as influences by the external measurement circuitry on a printed circuit board (PCB). The central topic of this work is the simulated and the measured EMI-induced offset voltage. Finally, we compare the different simulation methods with the real measurement, both in terms of offset deviation, as well as in terms of frequency deviation.

articleTitle: A Tunable Bandwidth and Center Frequency 6-Path BPF with Improved 3 $k^{th}$ Harmonics Rejection
abstract: In this work, the design of a multipath <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3k^{th}(k\in N)$</tex> harmonic rejection bandpass filter with tunable bandwidth and center frequency is proposed. The proposed filter architecture employs a nested filter structure with tunable non-identical loads in each filter to achieve the overall <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3k^{th}$</tex> harmonic rejection. This architecture also alleviates the need of an additional harmonic weighting stage to achieve an improved harmonic rejection. Six phase non-overlapping scheme is utlized to control the center frequency of a six path differential nested filter structure. The proposed harmonic rejection filter implemented in 28-nm is functional from the frequency range of 500 MHz to 2.9 GHz with channel bandwith tunable from 20 – 200 MHz. The overall harmonic rejection achieved at 1 G Hz is 58.6 dB. The achieved in-band <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$IIP_{3}$</tex> is −14 dBm and noise figure is 6–8 dB in the entire frequency band.

articleTitle: Ring Oscillator Based Smart Temperature Sensor Using All-Digital Sigma-Delta Modulator
abstract: In this work, an on-chip smart temperature sensor is presented. The design is based on a bias circuit providing two bias currents, two ring oscillators, an up/dow <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> counter, and a simple binary counter. One bias current has a positive temperature coefficient (PTAT), while the other bias current has a negative temperature coefficient (CTAT). The two currents bias the ring oscillators, producing the PTAT and the CTAT frequency clocks. The outputs of the two oscillators are combined and further processed using the all-digital implementation of time domain Sigma-Delta <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Sigma\triangle)$</tex> converter. The architecture is designed in 180-nm technology, and the nominal simulation results are presented, together with Monte Carlo analysis. The achieved accuracy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(3\sigma)$</tex> is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 5.4^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, within the temperature range from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$125^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, and the mean resolution is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.293^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A VCO-based Voice Activity Detection System for IoT applications
abstract: This paper shows a system level implementation of a Voice Activity Detector aimed at edge computing applications. The system is based on a voice band filter followed by a Manhattan norm calculator. It works with time encoded signals instead of charged capacitors or analog voltages. The advantages of this approach span from ultra low power consumption, to the suitability for deep sub-micron implementations, together with the possibility to fully synthesize the circuit using digital designing tools.

articleTitle: Generic Analog 8 Bit DAC IP Block in 28nm CMOS for the High Energy Physics Community
abstract: The High Energy Physics (HEP) microelectronic design community is leading a CMOS technology change from Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) designs in 130nm and 65nm to 28nm for the future upgrades of the High Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The technology change to a newer and one of the last planar bulk technologies allows benefiting from advances like higher intrinsic density and speed. The increased radiation hardness of 28nm makes this change also inevitable to withstand future radiation in the LHC experiments with levels of Total Ionizing Dose (TID) beyond 1 Grad. We present a generic 8-bit Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC) as an analog IP block for ASIC designs in the HEP community in 28nm CMOS technology and the design challenges of the novel technology in HEP ASICs.

articleTitle: A 130–160 GHz Frequency Tripler in a 130nm SiGe BiCMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents a D-band frequency tripler consisting of a frequency multiplication block and a power amplification block. The power amplifier (P A) follows the frequency multiplier, aiming to further increasing the output power of the desired generated harmonic. This wideband frequency tripler is implemented in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$130\text{nm\ SiGe}$</tex> BiCMOS technology. It exhibits a bandwidth of30 GHz (from 130 GHz to 160 GHz), an output power higher than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\ \text{dBm}$</tex> while the DC power consumption does not exceed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$310\text{mW}$</tex>.

articleTitle: FMCW radar system model enhanced with hardware coupling effects
abstract: The paper gives an overview of a characterization method that employs chirp linearity measurements and integrates them into an FMCW system model. The model is compared to system level measurements that utilize a delay line to emulate a radar target. Employing the delay line in this way implies various constraints, namely bandwidth limitation and a restriction to stationary targets. Good matching is observed between the model and the delay line measurements, however not in all areas of comparison. To complete the model, TX to RX coupling measurements are added. After this enhancement, good matching is observed in all areas.

articleTitle: A low-complexity DDS-based I/Q reference signal generation for capacitive sensing in 65nm CMOS
abstract: This work describes the results of the silicon evalu-ation of a direct digital synthesis (DDS) implementation, which was initially evaluated using virtual prototyping in SystemC AMS (IEEE 1666.1) and FPGA prototyping using VHDL (IEEE 1076). The block is part of a test chip produced in a 65nm CM OS technology. The result of the test chip is now available and allows the calibration of the model with measurement data. This model can then be re-used for future signal generation needs of capacitive sensor front-ends using carrier frequency based methods. Furthermore, the results of the design effort are presented and compared against another recently published design of a low complexity DDS in 65nm.

articleTitle: A Hall effect magnetic sensor with ratiometric output, utilizing a self-regulating chopped amplifier for compensation of offset, temperature and lifetime drift effects
abstract: This paper presents a Hall sensor for precise linear position detection, implemented in 130 nm BCD technology. The sensor contains temperature, mechanical stress and technology spread compensation and provides an analog output ratiometric to the external supply voltage. To comply with offset and noise requirements, the current spinning technique is applied to the Hall elements and chopping as well as an on-chip ripple reduction loop is implemented in the Hall signal amplifier. With this sensor concept an overall uncalibrated sensitivity error less than ± 5 % is achieved.

articleTitle: DUT Board Design Considerations for HV Application Reliability Testing of WBG Power Devices
abstract: This paper discusses design considerations of the printed circuit boards that carry WBG power devices for multi-channel HV application reliability tests. Different DUT board concepts are discussed regarding electrical and mechanical considerations as well as cooling strategies. All presented boards provide solutions for in-situ monitoring or intermittent static readouts of relevant device parameters. In the conclusion, a comparison of all main design properties is presented.

articleTitle: Novel Capacitance Sensing Measurement Technique for Human-Robot Co-existence
abstract: Nowadays, the need for safe human-robot-co-existence has become increasingly important. Therefore, the requirement to faithful detection of persons in the work arena of a robot is a prime concern to ensure human-safety. Capacitance based proximity sensors system is presented to measure the presence of objects and, hence, allow the detection of proximity of persons, enabling human robot collaboration. This paper presents the techniques for sensing tiny capacitance variations due to approaching objects among the presence of large parasitic capacitances. We also introduced a commn-mode (CM) compen-satory branch to reject rail-to-rail common-mode interference. In addition, we proposed the offset tolerant amplifier with the characteristics of low noise, high gain and wide-band operation. The proposed topology is designed, simulated and verified in 65 nm standard CMOS process.

articleTitle: Method of counter states encoding for passing the state jumps between asynchronous clock domains
abstract: The direct transmission of counter state between asynchronous clock domains in digital circuits requires a special coding of the states to protect the transmitted data from corruption, caused by asynchronous sampling of the multi-bit toggling value. The conventional Gray code is a known example of the code, allowing to transmit safely only adj acent state transitions. The proposed coding method allows to transmit safely any counter state jumps, limited by arbitrary predefined parameter. The potential application of the method is encoding of read- and write-pointers in asynchronous FIFOs with variable write-and/or read data sizes.
